Series::isinf¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::isinf() const -> Series
Series& Series::isinf_()

What It Does¶

isinf() returns a boolean mask that is true exactly where the value is either positive infinity or negative infinity.

This is narrower than isfinite() and different from isnan():

  • infinities are matched here

  • nan is not matched here

  • finite numbers are not matched here

Returns¶

Series A boolean Series with the same shape as self.

Gradient¶

isinf() is a boolean detector, not a differentiable numeric transform.

In-Place Form¶

isinf_() is the in-place sibling of isinf(): it computes the same result and writes it back into self directly — mutating it (and any other handle sharing the same storage) instead of allocating a new Series — then returns a reference to self.

auto x = pluss::make_series({1.0, std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity(), -std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity()});
x.isinf_();
std::cout << x;

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[3], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=3, contiguous=true)
data=[0, 1, 1]

Examples¶

Example 1. Both +inf and -inf are marked as true.

auto special = pluss::make_series({
    -std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity(),
    -1.0,
    std::numeric_limits<double>::quiet_NaN(),
    0.0,
    std::numeric_limits<double>::infinity(),
});

std::cout << special.isinf();

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[5], strides=[1], dtype=bool, platform=cpu, numel=5, contiguous=true)
data=[true, false, false, false, true]

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • nan does not count as infinity.

  • The output is a mask, not a repaired numeric result.

  • Use this when overflow-like conditions matter specifically, not when you want the broader non-finite test.

Summary¶

Use isinf() to isolate values that have blown out to positive or negative infinity.
